_meta.title: OpenAI Deployment Safety Hub — GPT-5.4 Thinking / GPT-5.5 Instant / ChatGPT Images 2.0 ingest
_meta.context: User-provided 3 deploymentsafety.openai.com pages: gpt-5-4-thinking (released March 5 2026), gpt-5-5-instant (released May 5 2026), chatgpt-images-2-0 (released April 21 2026). All 3 are OpenAI's official safety + Preparedness Framework evaluations under their post-System-Card 'living doc' framework. Cross-checked against DB: GPT-5.4 Thinking had 36 scores (mostly capability), GPT-5.4 Mini had 36, GPT-5.5 Instant had only 4, ChatGPT Images 2.0 + Thinking variant did NOT exist. Bio/preparedness benchmarks (virology_mcq, protocolqa_openended, tacit_knowledge_bio, troubleshootingbench, opqa, irregular_atomic_*) all exist in DB but lack scores for these specific models. Production safety 'not_unsafe' category scores are new benchmark family. ChatGPT Images 2.0 safety metrics (violative rate / detection rates / safe output rate) are an entirely new benchmark family.
_meta.rule: STRICT-ATTRIBUTION + PRESERVATION. All scores are verbatim from OpenAI's deployment safety pages. For GPT-5.4 Thinking, preserved existing scores (e.g. cyber_range 73.33, healthbench 62.6) where they match the page exactly; only added gaps. For GPT-5.4 Thinking CTF — DB has openai_ctf_professional 82.0 (likely earlier System Card snapshot, possibly pass@1); page reports pass@12 88.23%. PRESERVED 82.0 per strict-attribution; pass@12 not separately registered to avoid metric duplication. Tacit Knowledge + TroubleshootingBench: page shows base score + 'incl. refusals' variant — ingested base scores only (the refusal-adjusted variant is a safety-metric overlay, not a capability score). ChatGPT Images 2.0 safety percentages converted to the 0-100 scale (e.g. 96.1% combined detection rate stored as 96.1). 'Images Generated' raw counts (3112 / 6944) are sample sizes, not capability scores — recorded in _note but not as bench values.

models.name: ChatGPT Images 2.0
models._note: OpenAI multimodal image generation model, successor to GPT-4o Image Generation (1.0) and ChatGPT Images 1.5. Dense text rendering + high detail complexity. Powered by GPT Image 2 backend (see openai/gpt-image-2). Deployment safety baseline of 3,112 generated images evaluated.

models.name: ChatGPT Images 2.0 (Thinking)
models._note: Reasoning variant of ChatGPT Images 2.0. Achieves 3x lower violative output rate (6.7% vs 22.0%) at cost of higher remaining-undetected rate (12.5% vs 3.9%). Eval set 6,944 generated images.

scores._section: === ChatGPT Images 2.0 (released April 21 2026) — image safety pipeline (5 metrics) ===
scores._note: 685/3112 outputs flagged violative pre-safeguards. Higher than thinking variant (6.7%).
658/685 violative outputs caught by combined image+prompt layers.
3085/3112 final outputs pass as safe. Only 27 remaining-undetected violative outputs (0.9%).
598/685 image-layer detector recall.
529/685 prompt-layer detector recall.
464/6944 outputs flagged violative — 3.3x lower than non-thinking (22.0%). Reasoning steers away from policy edges.
406/464 caught by combined layers. Lower recall than non-thinking 96.1% (the remaining violative outputs are more subtle).
6886/6944 final outputs pass as safe. 58 remaining-undetected (12.5% of violative outputs).
357/464 image-layer recall.
222/464 prompt-layer recall — Thinking variant's harder-to-flag prompts evade prompt-layer detection more often.
